sign_off.blocking_on: Not ready for merge. The FIFTH review of this bundle was my own and found three proof-truth defects plus eight uncovered code properties; eleven new controls (G27-G37) were written for the latter. The sixth mutation round left TWO survivors, and in both cases the defect was in a control this lane had just written: G31's fixture put its fence markers inside a list item, where FENCE_RE never matches, so deleting the guard it named produced byte-identical output; and G19 could not observe the generic `contracts` refusal payload at all. Both are fixed and both mutations now die. That is vacuous control #14 in this lane, found by executing the mutation rather than by reading the test. The battery reported here is the UNION of every mutation run across all seven rounds (37), re-executed in full at this head: 37 of 37 detected, no survivors, no anchor misses. Every derived field in all three bundle files is now generated by one runner from that JSON and the live tree, because round 5 proved that hand-fixing leaves whatever the generator does not own. Four of five rounds have found a defect the previous round installed or missed, so a clean sixth review is not treated as a formality by this bundle.

review_threads.detail: The reserved set omitted guardrails, all four non-goals spellings, and required evidence/evidence, so a nested non-goal was both left in its acceptance ancestor and extracted as a non-goal. Fixed structurally: extraction and reservation now read one table (CONTRACT_FIELD_SPECS) and every extraction site goes through fieldSpec(). A flat list could not express non-goals' prefix matching in any case.

review_threads.subject: Honor fenced code while parsing headings
review_threads.detail: parseSections now tracks fenced blocks and requires at most three leading spaces. A second half not named in the report was found by assertion: sectionItems flattened a fenced block into one whitespace-collapsed line, putting a shell comment on the same line as the command it warns about. sectionItems is now fence-aware.
